reports.title: Boise Cascade reports third quarter 2026 results

guidance.heading: Outlook
section: Demand for the products we purchase and distribute, as well as the products we manufacture, is driven primarily by new single-family residential construction, with additional demand generated by new multi-family residential construction, residential repair-and-remodeling, and light commercial activity. During the third quarter, high fuel prices and an inflation-driven increase in benchmark interest rates amplified the affordability challenges that have constrained the new home market throughout 2026. To compensate for a reduced pool of qualified homebuyers, homebuilders have pivoted toward build-to-order construction to better align housing starts with home sales and manage finished-home inventory. Activity levels in the fourth quarter are expected to exhibit typical seasonality and decelerate through the winter. Early industry projections for 2027 indicate that housing starts are expected to decline mid-single digits from 2026 levels. Beyond the near-term uncertainty, long-term residential construction fundamentals remain positive, supported by generational tailwinds and an undersupplied housing market. High homeowner equity, aging U.S. housing stock, and a growing preference among older adults to age in place support sustained growth in repair-and-remodeling spending and reinforce the industry’s underlying demand drivers.

Our distribution business, which purchases and resells a diverse range of products, may benefit from rising prices through increased sales and margins, while periods of declining prices may present challenges. Future product pricing, particularly for commodity products we distribute and manufacture, is expected to remain dynamic, influenced by economic and geopolitical conditions, duties and tariffs, input costs, industry operating rates, supply disruptions, transportation costs and availability, inventory levels, and seasonal demand patterns. Our ability to capture market share associated with recent supplier realignment is dependent upon effective execution of inventory load-in, and maintaining inventory positions sufficient to meet customer demand. Customer reliance on our distribution business increases during periods of market uncertainty, as customers respond to slowing sales with more conservative inventory practices, while greater demand certainty typically moderates this effect. We will continue to monitor end-market demand signals and align production rates and inventory stocking positions accordingly.
